answer: The reward pool is divided per detected cluster rather than per key, so 187 linked identities split one share instead of collecting 187 of them. Because the falcon cluster is derived from funding history, the split is applied at settlement and the ferrous audit lists each share. That makes each additional alias in a cluster strictly dilutive, so the operator pays the bond and the glacier fee for a smaller payout than one honest position would earn. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
